5490.idn: Name in the source: mafa; family in the source: famille tchadique, branche centrale; groupe mafa

tn.quote: Il Y a une opposition de deux tons ponctuels haut / bas. Le ton haut (H) est marqué par un accent, le ton bas (B) est non-marqué: vézay "épervier" vézay "derrière" … Il y a très peu de paires minimales de ce genre dans le lexique. Considérant les deux derniers tons d'un nom, on peut distinguer des schèmes tonals isotones (H-H, B-B) ou hétérotone (H-B). Lexicalement, aucune schème ne se termine par une séquence bas-haut (B-H). Dans certaines constructions grammaticales apparait un ton modulé bas-haut (BH) sur la dernière syllabe.
tn.translation: There is an opposition of two level (punctual) tones, high / low. The high tone (H) is marked with an accent, the low tone (B) is unmarked: vézay 'sparrowhawk' / vezay 'behind' … There are very few minimal pairs of this kind in the lexicon. Considering the last two tones of a noun, one can distinguish isotone (H-H, L-L) or heterotone (H-L) tonal schemes. Lexically, no scheme ends in a low-high (L-H) sequence. In certain grammatical constructions a modulated low-high (LH) tone appears on the last syllable.
tn.cite: Barreteau, Daniel & Yves Le Bleis. 1990. Lexique mafa: langue de la famille tchadique parlée au Cameroun. (Études tchadiques, Monographies.) Paris: Éditions de l'ORSTOM / Librairie Orientaliste Paul Geuthner. 473 pp. IRD fdi:34119.
tn.locator: p.20, 'Éléments phonologiques' sec. 5 'Les tons'
tn.note: Two level tones, high and low, with a tone on each syllable; few lexical minimal pairs; a rising low-high surfaces only on final syllables in certain grammatical constructions.

tn.translation: 3.5. A fundamental difference appears at the level of lexical tones, where Mofu-Gudur stands out by the systematic presence of lexical tones preposed and postposed to the verb radical ... By comparison, Mbara is of a much more common type in that the lexical tone pattern is entirely contained within the radical itself. ... 3.7. They [subject person markers] have no tone of their own in Mbara and Mulwi, where the low or high tone of the preverbal person marker is a function of the perfective (accompli) or imperfective (inaccompli) aspect of the verb,

5496.prule: Primary stress falls on the first syllable of the root (the C1/sigma-1 position), which is the position of maximal phonemic contrast.
5496.quote: The first root syllable in Mpyemo is prominent. Contrast is at its maximum in the first root syllable and decreases as one moves rightwards. … The first root syllable has a special prominence, bearing stress and displaying the full inventory of phonemic contrasts, except for three marginal phonemes, (/ŋ, h, ɾ/). … Additionally, the C1 position is where primary stress is located.
5496.loc: p. 6 and p. 9, section 2.1 'Phonological structure of noun and verb roots' (table (2) lists 'Primary stress' under sigma-1)
5496.idn: Name in the source: Mpyemo; family in the source: Bantu A.80

tn.quote: Mpyemo has three phonetic pitch levels, but only two underlying tone heights: high and low. Two of the phonetic pitch levels are produced by unchanged high and low tones. The third is generated by a high tone raising (HTR) rule, where a high tone is raised to the “super-high” level when followed by a low tone. … Noun melodies consist of two tones per noun, regardless of the number of syllables in the noun. … Mpyemo nouns are thus divided into four major groups: H, L, H(L) and LH; and one minor group: HL.
tn.cite: Festen, Bradley D. 2018. Phonological Sketch of the Mpyemo Language. Bangui: ACATBA (Association Centrafricaine pour la Traduction de la Bible et l'Alphabétisation) & SIL International, SIL Central African Republic Service Group, November 2018. iv + 100 pp. (section 4 'Tone', pp. 26-31; Appendix B c. 1000-item tone-marked wordlist). CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
tn.locator: pp. 27-28, section 4 'Tone' (pp. 26-31)
tn.note: Two underlying tones, high and low, as word melodies (nouns H, L, H(L), LH, rare HL); a raising rule gives a third surface level, super-high; floating low tones; stress on the first root syllable.

tn.quote: Tones also play a distinctive role in the Ngamambo language. The H, L, M, HL, and LH tones are attested in this language, and the mid-tone is not marked. The H and L tones are commonly marked, and the contour tones are derived from tonological processes (usually, a floating tone from a deleted segment that spreads or docks to the preceding or following sound). These tones are expressed on monosyllabic, disyllabic, and polysyllabic words, and they equally bring about a difference in the meaning of words in the language.
tn.cite: Nyindem, Sirih Nagang Nancy. [2024]. A sociolinguistics impact of Ngamambo greeting culture and identity. AFO-A-KOM: Journal of Culture, Performing and Visual Arts 4(1), article 9, pp. 201-225. (University of Bamenda.)

tn.quote: This paper presents the Ngie (spoken in the Grasslands area of Cameroon) noun classes and tone system. Most Ngie nouns have a V,-C,(G)V,(C,) shape. The first vowel (i.e. the prefix) can either be i-, a-, or u- and can have either low or mid tone. The second vowel can have one of the following six tone shapes: low with downgliding before pause L [—_], low level L° [ —_], mid level [ —], high H [~ J], falling F [ ~] and rising R [ _~]. Out of the twelve theoretical tonal combinations, only two patterns are lacking: mid followed by level low and mid followed by rising tone.
tn.cite: Hombert, Jean-Marie. 1977. Noun classes and tone in Ngie [abstract]. UCLA Working Papers in Phonetics 36 (Studies on Tone, July 1977): 7. Los Angeles: UCLA Phonetics Laboratory. [Abstract of the paper published in L. M. Hyman (ed.) 1976, Studies in Bantu Tonology (SCOPIL 3), 3-21.]
tn.locator: p. 7 ('Abstracts' section); ('V,-C,(G)V,(C)' = V1-C1(G)V2(C2); bracketed glyphs = hand-drawn pitch marks)
tn.note: Noun prefixes carry low or mid tone; the stem vowel has one of six tone shapes: low (gliding down before pause), level low, mid, high, falling, rising; 10 of 12 prefix+stem patterns occur (abstract).

sources.cite: Li Shengfu 李生福. 1996. 彝语南部方言研究 [Research on the Southern dialect of Yi]. Beijing: Minzu chubanshe 民族出版社. 306 pp.
sources.text: "重音、轻音、长短音和语调是音质以外的语音特征在语言中的几种主要表现形式。声调主要是指语言中每一音节所固有的能 ... 语言都有声调。彝语中的每个音节都有声调。但各地的声调数量多少不等,一般有 3-5 个声调。彝语南部方言双柏话有高平、中平、低降三个声调。彝语除了有声调外,有些音节还带有表意重音或表情重音。重音是相连的音节中某个音节发音突出的现象,它出现在句子中,同时也出现在某些语言的单词中。如云南双柏彝语: do2'love33 “得了! ”或“够了! ” (看见异常情况时所发出来的自然感叹声或紧急呼声)凉山彝语 [..]33 mo33 “阿妈! ” (遇到危险时的惊呼声)这类摹描自然声响的象声词和叹词,都带表意重音或表情重音。另外,彝语的表意重音有区别词汇意义和语法意义的作用。[双柏彝语声调表 follows: 55 高平 mo (高、实、竹), sa (黄、长、蛇、金); 33 中平 do (耕、借、五、鱼), dzo (吃、犁、闻); 21 低降 thu (白、厚、银), x (海、湖、拿、飘)]" (pp. 14-15, chapter 彝语南部方言语音, the 声调/重音 paragraph immediately preceding the 双柏彝语声调表; page numbers rest only on the Google page-break marke…

5501.idn: Name in the source: 新平彝语 (Xinping Yi); the statement concerns a variety of this language

tn.quote: 新平彝语共有 35 个声母，18 个韵母，3 个声调，有非常整齐的松紧音对立，音系如下： … 声调（3） 第一调 33 第二调 21 第三调 55 新平彝语 33 调和 21 调都存在松紧音对立，而 55 调没有，为方便起见，本文将 33、21 调与松紧音的搭配分别处理为两个声调。 … 故本文将新平彝语声调系统一共处理为 5 个调位，即 33 松、33 紧、21 松、21 紧、55 松。 … 这里将新平彝语基频的区别性特征定义为三类： 1、2 调为中平，3、4 调为低降，5 调为高平。
tn.translation: Xinping Yi has 35 initials, 18 finals and 3 tones, with a very regular tense/lax opposition; the system is: ... Tones (3): tone 1 = 33, tone 2 = 21, tone 3 = 55. In Xinping Yi the 33 and 21 tones both carry the tense/lax opposition while 55 does not; for convenience this paper treats the pairings of 33 and 21 with tense and lax as two tones each. ... So the Xinping Yi tone system is treated as 5 tonal categories in all: 33 lax, 33 tense, 21 lax, 21 tense, 55 lax. ... Here the distinctive F0 features of Xinping Yi are defined as three classes: tones 1, 2 mid level; tones 3, 4 low falling; tone 5 high level.
tn.cite: Ye, Zehua 叶泽华. 2010. 新平彝语松紧嗓音研究 [A study of tense and lax phonation in Xinping Yi]. In 语音乐律研究报告 2010 (Status Report of Phonetic and Music Research 2010), 105-122. Beijing: 北京大学中文系语言学实验室.

tn.note: Three tones: mid level 33, low falling 21, high level 55; tense vs lax phonation contrasts under 33 and 21 (the author counts 5 tone-phonation categories); EGG and F0 study; nothing on stress.

variants.name: Shuangbai Yi 双柏彝语 (as described by Li Shengfu 李生福; formerly filed under the code of Ache)
variants.prule: No word-stress position stated. Every Yi syllable bears a tone; the Shuangbai speech of the Southern dialect has three tones, high level 55, mid level 33, low falling 21 (双柏彝语声调表). Besides tone, 'some syllables' carry 'semantic stress' (表意重音) or 'expressive stress' (表情重音): prominence of one syllable among adjacent syllables, occurring in sentences and also in words, exemplified by interjections/onomatopoeia (Shuangbai do2'love33 'enough!/that's it!'; Liangshan [..]33 mo33 'Mother!', first syllable not legible in the excerpt), and said to distinguish lexical and grammatical meaning. Which syllable bears it is not stated in the readable text.
variants.quote: 重音、轻音、长短音和语调是音质以外的语音特征在语言中的几种主要表现形式。声调主要是指语言中每一音节所固有的能 ... 语言都有声调。彝语中的每个音节都有声调。但各地的声调数量多少不等,一般有 3-5 个声调。彝语南部方言双柏话有高平、中平、低降三个声调。彝语除了有声调外,有些音节还带有表意重音或表情重音。重音是相连的音节中某个音节发音突出的现象,它出现在句子中,同时也出现在某些语言的单词中。如云南双柏彝语: do2'love33 “得了! ”或“够了! ” (看见异常情况时所发出来的自然感叹声或紧急呼声)凉山彝语 [..]33 mo33 “阿妈! ” (遇到危险时的惊呼声)这类摹描自然声响的象声词和叹词,都带表意重音或表情重音。另外,彝语的表意重音有区别词汇意义和语法意义的作用。[双柏彝语声调表 follows: 55 高平 mo (高、实、竹), sa (黄、长、蛇、金); 33 中平 do (耕、借、五、鱼), dzo (吃、犁、闻); 21 低降 thu (白、厚、银), x (海、湖、拿、飘)]
variants.loc: pp. 14-15, chapter 彝语南部方言语音, the 声调/重音 paragraph immediately preceding the 双柏彝语声调表; page numbers rest only on the Google page-break marker '14.' that sits between 凉山 and 彝语 in excerpt.
variants.cite: Li Shengfu 李生福. 1996. 彝语南部方言研究 [Research on the Southern dialect of Yi]. Beijing: Minzu chubanshe 民族出版社. 306 pp.

variants.note: Filed under the code of Ache (ache1244) until V9.20; the description is of Shuangbai Yi 双柏彝语, which Glottolog lists as Northwestern Nisu (nort2718). ache1244 Ache (Nisoid > Unclassified Nisoid) lists only Ache / Yi, Ache and has no dialects; neither Shuangbai nor Southern Yi appears there.

tn.quote: 声调主要是指语言中每一音节所固有的能区别意义的声音的高低和升降。 … 彝语中的每个音节都有声调。但各地的声调数量多少不等,一般有 3-5 个声调。彝语南部方言双柏话有高平、中平、低降三个声调。彝语除了有声调外,有些音节还带有表意重音或表情重音。 … 双柏彝语声调表调值调号例词 55 1 mo ” (高、实、竹) sa ” (黄、长、蛇、金) (高平调) 33 (中平调) ᅥ Do33 (耕、借、五、鱼) dzo33 (吃、犁、闻) 33 21 ↓ (低降调) thu2 (白、厚、银) x21 (海、湖、拿、飘)
tn.translation: Tone chiefly means the meaning-distinguishing pitch height and rise or fall inherent in every syllable of a language. ... Every syllable in Yi has a tone. But the number of tones differs from place to place, generally 3-5 tones. The Shuangbai speech of the Southern dialect of Yi has three tones: high level, mid level and low falling. Besides tone, some syllables in Yi also carry semantic stress or expressive stress. ... Shuangbai Yi tone table (tone value / tone mark / example words): 55 (high level tone) mo (tall, solid, bamboo), sa (yellow, long, snake, gold); 33 (mid level tone) Do33 (till, borrow, five, fish), dzo33 (eat, plough, smell); …
tn.cite: Li Shengfu 李生福. 1996. 彝语南部方言研究 [Research on the Southern dialect of Yi]. Beijing: Minzu chubanshe 民族出版社. 306 pp. (ISBN 7105027037)
tn.locator: pp. 14-15, chapter 彝语南部方言语音, 声调 paragraph + 双柏彝语声调表
tn.note: Three tones on every syllable: high level 55, mid level 33, low falling 21; no rising tone. Some syllables (interjections etc.) also carry a 'semantic/expressive stress'; numerals show tone sandhi. Checked against the source (tone consistency check, 2026-09-23): evidence unstated -> impressionistic (pp. 14-15, 双柏彝语声调表).

refs.ref: Struthers-Young, Anthony. 2026 (ms, dated May 7, 2026). "Northern Toussian." Submitted to Journal of the International Phonetic Association (JIPA Illustration; Djigouera dialect). 38 pp. https://ling.auf.net/lingbuzz/010271

5502.loc: section 'Tone', p. 18 (inventory and table); downstep sentence p. 24
5502.idn: Name in the source: Northern Toussian; family in the source: Niger-Congo; the Toussian languages are of uncertain genetic affiliation, originally classified as Gur (Mabia), grouped with the 'peripheral Gur' languages

tn.quote: Northern Toussian has three level tones: a high tone (á), mid tone (ā), and low tone (à). Additionally, it has six lexical contour tones, HM (a᷇), HL (â), LH (ǎ), LHL (ǎ`), LHM (ǎ¯), and HLH (â´), though the HLH contour is only attested in one word, bê´ ‘again.’ I analyze the contour tones as being comprised of two or more of the level tones. … Downstep is frequent in the language, and both H and M tones can be downstepped.
tn.cite: Struthers-Young, Anthony. 2026 (ms, dated May 7, 2026). "Northern Toussian." Submitted to Journal of the International Phonetic Association (JIPA Illustration; Djigouera dialect). 38 pp. https://ling.auf.net/lingbuzz/010271
tn.locator: section 'Tone', p. 18 (inventory and table); downstep sentence p. 24
tn.note: Three level tones (high, mid, low); a syllable may carry contours HM, HL, LH, LHL, LHM, HLH, analysed as sequences of levels; downstep of H and M, incl. from a floating L grammatical tone.

refs.ref: Nguyễn Phương Linh & Nguyễn Ngọc Bình. 2025. Hệ thống thanh điệu tiếng Nùng Xuồng (tại thôn Thăm Noọng, xã Tát Ngà, huyện Mèo Vạc, tỉnh Hà Giang). Từ điển học & Bách khoa thư 2025(5): 7-13.

5504.loc: §5 Thảo luận, p. 12 and §6 Kết luận, pp. 12-13; pitch values in Bảng 2 p. 10
5504.idn: Name in the source: Nùng Xuồng (tiếng Nùng Xuồng); family in the source: tiểu nhóm Tai trung tâm, nhánh Kam-Tai, ngữ hệ Tai-Kadai (Central Tai subgroup, Kam-Tai branch, Tai-Kadai family); 'nhóm địa phương của dân tộc Nùng'; the statement concerns a variety of this language

tn.quote: Nùng Xuồng và tiếng Việt đều có cấu trúc 6+2: 6 thanh trong âm tiết không đóng và 2 thanh chỉ ở âm tiết đóng. … bài viết đã xác định được hệ thống thanh điệu của tiếng Nùng Xuồng bao gồm sáu thanh điệu cơ bản và hai thanh điệu nhập. Kết quả cho thấy hệ thống thanh điệu tiếng Nùng Xuồng có tính khu biệt rõ ràng, được tổ chức theo cặp đối lập cả về âm vực (cao - thấp) và âm điệu (bằng - trắc), đồng thời phản ánh đầy đủ các dạng vận động của thanh điệu hình tuyến như đi lên, đi xuống, bằng phẳng hay gãy khúc.
tn.translation: Nùng Xuồng and Vietnamese both have a 6+2 structure: 6 tones in non-closed syllables and 2 tones only in closed syllables. … the article has established that the tone system of Nùng Xuồng comprises six basic tones and two checked (nhập) tones. The results show that the Nùng Xuồng tone system is clearly distinctive, organised in opposed pairs both in register (high - low) and in contour (level - oblique), and at the same time reflects all the movement types of linear tone: rising, falling, level or broken.
tn.cite: Nguyễn Phương Linh & Nguyễn Ngọc Bình. 2025. Hệ thống thanh điệu tiếng Nùng Xuồng (tại thôn Thăm Noọng, xã Tát Ngà, huyện Mèo Vạc, tỉnh Hà Giang). Từ điển học & Bách khoa thư 2025(5): 7-13.
tn.locator: §5 Thảo luận, p. 12 and §6 Kết luận, pp. 12-13; pitch values in Bảng 2 p. 10
tn.note: Six tones on non-checked syllables (33 level, 221 low falling, 455 high rising, 343 rise-fall, 35 rising, 51 high falling) plus two short checked tones (445, 211) in /p t k/ syllables; Praat F0.

5504.cfw: One first-hand description of the tone system, checked against the source; 8 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

refs.ref: Hyman, Larry M. 2014. How to study a tone language, with exemplification from Oku (Grassfields Bantu, Cameroon). Language Documentation & Conservation 8: 525-562.

5505.loc: pp. 544-545, section 4 'Stage III: Developing a tonal analysis', summary (25a) and following paragraphs
5505.idn: Name in the source: Oku; family in the source: Grassfields Bantu, Ring subgroup

tn.quote: (25) a. surface contrasts i. three tone heights (H, M, L) ii. a level L˚ tone which contrasts with L only before pause iii. falling contours: HM, HL, ML iv. no rising contours, with one exception (ncìí ‘chief’s house’) … from the presence of HM, HL, and ML contours, it is obvious that Oku tone cannot be analyzed as privative. … I will now suggest that the underlying system is /H/ vs. /L/ in Oku, and that all M tones are derived, as is the contrast between L˚ and L.
tn.cite: Hyman, Larry M. 2014. How to study a tone language, with exemplification from Oku (Grassfields Bantu, Cameroon). Language Documentation & Conservation 8: 525-562.
tn.locator: pp. 544-545, section 4 'Stage III: Developing a tonal analysis', summary (25a) and following paragraphs
tn.note: Two underlying tones, /H/ vs /L/; surface H, M, L, a level L˚ and falling HM, HL, ML contours are derived by rule (M = H lowered after L); floating H and L tones; noun roots /H, L, HL, LH/.

refs.ref: Smolders, Joshua A. G. 2019. Nominal and verbal number in Bilugu Opo. Studies in African Linguistics 48(1): 133-184. doi:10.32473/sal.v48i1.114929

5506.loc: sec. 1.5 Phonological Overview, pp. 139-140 with Table 5 'Lexical tone contrast in Opo (Bilugu only)'
5506.idn: Name in the source: Opo; family in the source: Koman (with Gwama, Komo, Uduk, Gule); Nilo-Saharan > Satellite-Core > Core > Koman per Bender 1997/Ethnologue…; the statement concerns a variety of this language (Opo (Bilugu dialect); a.k.a. Opuuo, Tʼapo [lgn])

tn.quote: Tone in Opo has a high lexical and grammatical functional load. According to my analysis there are four levels of phonemic tone in Bilugu: low (L), mid (M), high (H), and extra‑high (X). Extra-high is attested only on a subset of the vowels: /i u a/. The number of phonemic tone levels in the other dialects has not been fully analyzed, but based on current data there are possibly only three. Table 5 below gives evidence of four levels of contrast on monosyllabic, monomorphemic nouns in a M_H environment, using the frame /tā __ tɔ́n/ 'It is a big __'.
tn.cite: Smolders, Joshua A. G. 2019. Nominal and verbal number in Bilugu Opo. Studies in African Linguistics 48(1): 133-184. doi:10.32473/sal.v48i1.114929
tn.locator: sec. 1.5 Phonological Overview, pp. 139-140 with Table 5 'Lexical tone contrast in Opo (Bilugu only)'
tn.note: Four level tones in the Bilugu dialect: low, mid, high, extra-high (extra-high only on /i u a/); syllable contours treated as two-tone sequences; other dialects possibly three levels.

refs.ref: De Boeck, L.-B. 1949. Note sur la langue des Apakabete. Bulletin des Séances, Institut Royal Colonial Belge XX(4): 834-843.

5507.loc: sec. 1 p. 835 and sec. 3 'La tonologie des noms' pp. 840-841; verb tone pp. 842-843
5507.idn: Name in the source: Apakabete (la langue des Apakabete); family in the source: Not classified by the author: he reports the view (Van der Kercken, Vanhouteghem via Van Bulck) that it 'serait un dialecte Ngbandi ayant subi des influences Ngombe'…

tn.quote: le groupe oriental emploie des tons nettement moyens, tandis que le groupe occidental ne les a pas. De plus il semble que ce soient surtout les tons descendants — qui sont très courts — du groupe occidental qui sont prononcés comme des tons moyens en Bondzoki. … Nous n ’avons trouvé que les mélodies suivantes. Le radical du nom (avec son suffixe) a les tons: haut-bas: par exemple, h'so, néme, pési, kéme; … haut-descendant … par exemple, mi'kî, kôko, kâse; … bas-descendant … par exemple, ekongâ; bas-haut: par exemple, nyame, sopó, nokó,
tn.translation: the eastern group uses clearly mid tones, whereas the western group does not have them. Moreover it seems to be mainly the falling tones - which are very short - of the western group that are pronounced as mid tones in Bondzoki. ... We found only the following melodies. The noun radical (with its suffix) has the tones: high-low: e.g. h'so, néme, pési, kéme; high-falling ... e.g. mi'kî, kôko, kâse; low-falling ... e.g. ekongâ; low-high: e.g. nyame, sopó, nokó,
tn.cite: De Boeck, L.-B. 1949. Note sur la langue des Apakabete. Bulletin des Séances, Institut Royal Colonial Belge XX(4): 834-843.
tn.locator: sec. 1 p. 835 and sec. 3 'La tonologie des noms' pp. 840-841; verb tone pp. 842-843
tn.note: High, low and a short falling tone (the eastern group has mid where the western has falling); noun stems keep fixed melodies HL, H-falling, L-falling, LH; verb roots keep their tone; no count given.

refs.ref: Hornéy, Christina Scotte. 2019. Tonal Variation in Pyen. Journal of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society (JSEALS) 12(1): 12-24. Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press. http://hdl.handle.net/10524/52442

5508.loc: p.22, sec. 7 Summary; cf. sec. 5 Tone patterns p.18 minimal set /cʰə̀/ 'dig' vs /cʰə̄/ 'pick flowers' vs /cʰə́/ 'sing'
5508.idn: Name in the source: Pyen; family in the source: Bisoid subgroup of the Southern Ngwi branch, Tibeto-Burman

tn.quote: Pyen has three contrastive tones, high, mid, and low, with stop-final syllables taking only mid and low tones. The low tone has falling pitch, the other tones are fairly level. Verb stems and nouns carry all three tones; the majority of these must take the mid-tone prefix /āŋ-/ … Suffixes have either high or low tone, but for at least three verb suffixes the tone is unspecified. These are the markers /-ne/ ‘imperfective’, /-ɟi/ ‘cited form’, and /-kʲa/ ‘place.where’, occurring with both high or low tone since their realization depends on the tone of the preceding verb stem or suffix.
tn.cite: Hornéy, Christina Scotte. 2019. Tonal Variation in Pyen. Journal of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society (JSEALS) 12(1): 12-24. Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press. http://hdl.handle.net/10524/52442
tn.locator: p.22, sec. 7 Summary; cf. sec. 5 Tone patterns p.18 minimal set /cʰə̀/ 'dig' vs /cʰə̄/ 'pick flowers' vs /cʰə́/ 'sing'
tn.note: Three contrastive tones, high, mid and low (low slightly falling), on stems and nouns; stop-final syllables take only mid or low; three toneless verb suffixes are high after high/mid, low after low.

5508.cfw: One first-hand description of the tone system, checked against the source; 3 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

refs.ref: Sarmah, Priyankoo. 2009. Tone systems of Dimasa and Rabha: a phonetic and phonological study. PhD dissertation, University of Florida.

5509.loc: ch. 7 Conclusion, 'Tone Inventories' p. 136 and 'General Tone Assignment Pattern' p. 140
5509.idn: Name in the source: Rabha; family in the source: Bodo-Garo subfamily of the Tibeto-Burman language family (Tibeto-Burman a part of Sino-Tibetan)

tn.quote: As far as the number of tones is concerned, this study concludes that in both Dimasa and Rabha, there are three phonological tones or tonemes. … Depending on the shape of the pitch contour, it is assessed that Dimasa and Rabha have a rising (R), falling (F) and a mid-level (M) tone. … in both Dimasa and Rabha underived words, only one lexical tone is underlyingly specified and that lexical tone is associated with the rightmost syllable of word. Any syllable that is devoid of an underlying lexical tone is assigned an unmarked mid-level tone …
tn.cite: Sarmah, Priyankoo. 2009. Tone systems of Dimasa and Rabha: a phonetic and phonological study. PhD dissertation, University of Florida.
tn.locator: ch. 7 Conclusion, 'Tone Inventories' p. 136 and 'General Tone Assignment Pattern' p. 140
tn.note: Three tones, rising, falling and mid-level (acoustic study); one lexical tone per word on its final syllable, other syllables default mid; a suffix keeps its tone and the stem goes mid.

refs.ref: Singha, Y. Arunima. 2017. A Descriptive Grammar of Reang. Ph.D. thesis, Department of Linguistics, Assam University, Silchar. xxi+360 pp. http://hdl.handle.net/10603/368135

5510.loc: ch. 3 Phonology, sec. 3.2 'Tones' with Table no 3 'Tones in Reang', pp. 24-25
5510.idn: Name in the source: Reang; family in the source: Bodo-Garo sub-group of the Tibeto-Burman sub family (Benedict 1972; central Bodo-Garo group per Jacquesson 2006, 'a distinct language', not a dialect of Kokborok)

tn.quote: 3.2. Tones Like other Tibeto-Burman languages, Reang is a tone language in which a change in the pitch of the syllable corresponds to a change in its meaning. Reang has two lexical tones namely high and low. (i) Low: the tension of the vocal cords in the production of a syllable is relatively low, causing a low pitch. The low tone is marked by the symbol / ˋ/. (ii) High: the tension of the vocal cords in the production of a syllable is relatively high, causing a high pitch. It is represented by the symbol / ʹ/. … ̸ kəˋtúŋ̸ „wool‟ ̸ kəˋtùŋ ̸ „hot‟ ̸ hór ̸ „fire‟ ̸ hòr ̸ „night‟ …
tn.cite: Singha, Y. Arunima. 2017. A Descriptive Grammar of Reang. Ph.D. thesis, Department of Linguistics, Assam University, Silchar. xxi+360 pp. http://hdl.handle.net/10603/368135
tn.locator: ch. 3 Phonology, sec. 3.2 'Tones' with Table no 3 'Tones in Reang', pp. 24-25
tn.note: Two lexical tones, high and low, marked with acute and grave; a change in the pitch of a syllable changes meaning (e.g. hór 'fire' vs hòr 'night'). Nothing is said about word stress.

5511.idn: Name in the source: ロロ語ニー方言 (Nyi方言); family in the source: Lolo系の諸言語 (Lolo languages), ロロ・ビルマ諸語 (Lolo-Burmese), シナ・チベット語族 (Sino-Tibetan)

tn.quote: まず，ここで取り上げるロロ語ニー方言，アヒ方言，ハニ語，リス語およびビルマ語の声調体系を掲げて，比較される対象を明らかにしておきたい6）。 [table] ロロ語，ニー方言 1. 高平型 55 2. 半高型 44 3. 中平型 33 4. 低平型 11 5. 短平型? 2͡2 五声 … 6）… 以下の声調表記は，ニー・アヒ・ハニ語は声調型を用い，リス語とビルマ語は声調類で示した。声調類は，対立する声調の種類を単に序数で代表させたものであるが，声調型は，1から5までの段階を設けて，その高低（register）および昇降（contour）関係を具体的に示す方法を用いて表記した。たとえば，35は3位の段階から5位まで上昇する型をあらわし，33は中位の平板型を示すなど。
tn.translation: First I set out the tone systems of the Lolo Nyi dialect, the Ahi dialect, Hani, Lisu and Burmese taken up here, to make clear what is being compared.6) [table] Lolo, Nyi dialect: 1. high-level type 55, 2. half-high type 44, 3. mid-level type 33, 4. low-level type 11, 5. short-level type ˀ22; five tones ... 6) ... In the tone notation below, tone types (values) are used for Nyi, Ahi and Hani, and tone classes for Lisu and Burmese. Tone classes simply represent the contrasting tones by ordinal numbers, whereas tone types are written with a five-step scale, 1 to 5, showing concretely their height (register) and rise-fall (contour); e.g. …

5512.idn: Name in the source: séki (seki, B21); family in the source: groupe Kota-Kele (B20), bantu (Guthrie zone B)

tn.quote: Sur le plan tonal, le seki manifeste trois (3) tonèmes selon M. E. Gningah (2010, p. 142), à savoir: un tonème /H/ et un tonème /B/ respectivement représenté par / ʹ/ et / ˋ/. Mais aussi, un tonème descendant /D/ noté /^/. Les tonèmes ont une fonction distinctive dans la langue. … les deux tons, H et B, apparaissent dans toutes les positions (initiale, médiane, finale) … Le tonème descendant quant à lui a été répertorié exclusivement en position finale des dissyllabiques /mbándzâ/ « bambou » ou dans les monosyllabiques /mbô/ « plante du pied ».
tn.translation: On the tonal level, Seki shows three (3) tonemes according to M. E. Gningah (2010, p. 142), namely a /H/ toneme and a /L/ toneme written with acute and grave respectively, and also a falling toneme /D/ written /^/. The tonemes have a distinctive function in the language. … the two tones H and L appear in all positions (initial, medial, final) … The falling toneme has been recorded only in final position of disyllables /mbándzâ/ 'bamboo' or in monosyllables /mbô/ 'sole of the foot'.
tn.cite: Koumbi Mabiti, Glenn Aymar. 2025. Phonologie diachronique des parlers du groupe Kota-Kele (B20) pour un affinement des embranchements internes. Thèse de doctorat, Université Omar Bongo (Libreville), dir. Y. Nzang Bie. 381 pp. HAL tel-04957912.
tn.locator: p. 66 (examples continue p. 67), section I.2.2.1.3 'Organisation des tonèmes'
tn.note: Three distinctive tonemes: high, low and a rare falling tone found only word-finally or on monosyllables; H and L occur in every position. Description relayed from Gningah 2010; nothing on stress.

5514.idn: Name in the source: Tai Nuea; family in the source: Tai-Kadai languages within the Sino-Tibetan language family

tn.quote: Tai Nuea has nine tones: six unchecked and three checked. Among the unchecked tones, there are two level tones: a mid-level tone (T33) and a high-level tone (T55). … Additionally, there are two falling tones: a mid-falling tone (T31) and a high-falling tone (T51). … There are also two rising tones, T24 and T35. … There are three checked tones in Tai Nuea. T23 is a rising tone, with the f0 contour moving from low to mid … T31 is a falling tone, with the f0 contour moving from mid to low … T55 is a high-level tone, aligned with the tonal pattern of the unchecked tone T55.
tn.cite: Wang, Lu, Binghao Wang & Yao Lu. 2026. Tai Nuea. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 56, e21, 1-17. doi:10.1017/S0025100326101108

5515.idn: Name in the source: Ngoni; family in the source: Bantu (Niger-Congo); Bantu N10 Manda group in Guthrie's classification (N12)

tn.quote: Before discussing the data, a short description of the Ngoni structure is given as a background. Ngoni is a 5 vowel Bantu language. The consonant system comprises 24 phonemes. … The orthography in this study follows Ngonyani. Ngoni has two pitch levels, high and low, but no lexical tone. The basic pattern assigns high tone to the antepenultimate syllable. This pattern is now frequently violated due to influences of other languages (ibid:13).
tn.cite: Rosendal, Tove & Gastor Mapunda. 2014. Is the Tanzanian Ngoni language threatened? A survey of lexical borrowing from Swahili. Journal of Multilingual and Multicultural Development 35(3): 271-288.
tn.locator: author manuscript p. 8, section 'Results' (opening structural sketch), (published version JMMD 35(3): 271-288)
tn.note: No lexical tone: two pitch levels (high, low), with high assigned by rule to the antepenultimate syllable (after Ngonyani 2003); this pattern is now often violated under contact influence.

5515.cfw: Known only second-hand: Rosendal & Mapunda 2014 reports the tone system after another work; the primary description was not read.

5516.idn: Name in the source: Tay (Dao Ngan Tay, DN); family in the source: Tai: a 'B-language' (Theraphan 1994: reflexes show voiced stops for Proto-Tai voiced stops)…; the statement concerns a variety of this language

tn.quote: DN has five tones on open syllables (those with final, vowel, semivowel and nasal): 1. level, slightly higher than mid: naa! ‘thick’, khaai ‘leg’, ?dong1 ‘east’, maai ‘dog’ 2. falling, slightly lower than mid: naa\ ‘rice field’, daangi ‘road’, maa\ ‘to come’ 3. high rise: taang1 'window', mai4 ‘widow’, naa‘ ‘mother's younger sister’ ’ 4. low fall and rise: naad ‘face’, khaad ‘to kill’, maM ‘bamboo shoot’ 5. low level: doyJ ‘stomach, gaaJ 'to tell’, maa! ‘horse’, mai] ‘tree’ Glottalisation is a feature of low pitch in Tones 4 and 5 with corresponding vowel shortening in Tone 5.
tn.cite: Ross, Peter A. 1996. Dao Ngan Tay: A B-language in Vietnam. Mon-Khmer Studies 25: 133-139.
tn.note: Five tones on live syllables: level above mid, falling below mid, high rising, low falling-rising, low level (4-5 glottalised); checked syllables take tones 3/4, varying with 1/5. Nothing on stress.
